s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive neurological decline with motor and speech impairment
salient_findings: Episodes of spasms and tremors in the right hand and forearm
Extensive nonenhancing lesions in the bilateral cerebral hemispheres
key_facts: Woman in her mid-60s
Initial presentation with episodes of spasms and tremors in the right hand and forearm
Underwent carpal tunnel release surgery
Tremors recurred 7 months later
Referred to a neurologist
Developed progressive right-sided weakness over 3 months
Developed dysarthria, hand tremors, slurred speech, and gait instability
Brain MRI showed hyperintensities throughout the bilateral cerebral hemispheric white matter
Brain MRI showed absence of contrast enhancement
Brain biopsy revealed CD19+ CD20+ BCL6+ MUM-1+ lymphoma cells
Cerebrospinal fluid presence of lymphoma cells
Bone marrow negative for lymphoma cells

shortlist.label: Primary Central Nervous System Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Brain biopsy revealed CD19+ CD20+ BCL6+ MUM-1+ lymphoma cells and cerebrospinal fluid presence of lymphoma cells

shortlist.label: Intravascular Large B-Cell Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive neurological decline with motor and speech impairment, and presence of lymphoma cells in cerebrospinal fluid

shortlist.label: Neurolymphomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Brain MRI showed hyperintensities throughout the bilateral cerebral hemispheric white matter and presence of lymphoma cells in cerebrospinal fluid

shortlist.label: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Brain MRI showed hyperintensities throughout the bilateral cerebral hemispheric white matter, although absence of contrast enhancement and lymphoma cells suggest a lower likelihood

shortlist.label: Corticobasal Degeneration
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive right-sided weakness, dysarthria, hand tremors, slurred speech, and gait instability, although lymphoma findings make this less likely

raw.rationale: The presence of lymphoma cells in the cerebrospinal fluid and the brain biopsy, along with the imaging findings of hyperintensities in the bilateral cerebral hemispheric white matter without contrast enhancement, are consistent with Primary Central Nervous System Lymphoma.

rejected.label: Intravascular Large B-Cell Lymphoma
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with skin lesions, fever, and neurological symptoms, but the imaging findings and biopsy results do not support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Neurolymphomatosis
rejected.why: While this condition involves lymphoma cells in the nervous system, the clinical presentation and imaging findings are more consistent with Primary Central Nervous System Lymphoma.

rejected.label: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy
rejected.why: This condition is caused by a viral infection and typically presents with asymmetric white matter lesions, which is not consistent with the bilateral and symmetric lesions seen in this case.

rejected.label: Corticobasal Degeneration
rejected.why: This is a neurodegenerative disorder that presents with asymmetric parkinsonism, dystonia, and myoclonus, which is not consistent with the clinical presentation and imaging findings of this case.
